label: Sub Pop Records
release_notes: Caspian Halliwell - lead vocals, guitar, songwriter; RJ Santos - steel guitar (Sub Pop and press profiles). The two met as neighbors in New Orleans' Holy Cross neighborhood. Halliwell's earlier bands include Blackbird Raum and Scissorbills; Santos played in Cajun and country bands.
No producer, studio or other personnel credits published as of Oct. 18.

Sound: garage rock, country and traditional folk, with steel guitar over shuffling drums (Pitchfork, via Sub Pop). Earlier songs lean on drum machines, slide guitar, organ and a drawling baritone (Stereogum).
Sub Pop debut, after two earlier 2026 albums, Blame the Clown (Chain Smoking Records) and Florida Water Blues (Going Underground).
Press materials call the songs anthems of longing and disappointment, from a brutal breakup to snitching ex-friends.

pull_quotes.text: like an old jukebox standard that you’re hearing for the first time

draft_comment: Out Nov. 6. New Orleans garage rock with steel guitar and a country drawl, from a duo that keeps making albums. Both screened tracks are clean, the other eleven are unscreened, so mind the FCCs.

tracks.title: Stalks
tracks.notes: Drum machine, sha-la-la guitar riffs, organ swirls and non-stop slide guitar under a hard-drawling baritone (Stereogum). Fuzzy, rock and roll feel (Song Bar). Toggles between flirty and frustrated (Sub Pop).

tracks.title: When We First Met
tracks.notes: Short and frantic: hopped-up guitar with raw amp distortion, steel guitar and roaring vocals (Still Listening, Scientists of Sound, Paste). Shout-along feel (Sub Pop).
